---
title: "Coming from R"
subtitle: "Line-by-line translation from the OHDSI package"
---

This package is a port of
[EmpiricalCalibration](https://github.com/OHDSI/EmpiricalCalibration) v3.1.4.
Function names, argument names, argument order and defaults are unchanged, so
most R code translates by changing `<-` to `=` and `$` to `.`.

## Side by side

::: {.panel-tabset}

## R

```r
library(EmpiricalCalibration)

data(sccs)
negatives <- sccs[sccs$groundTruth == 0, ]
positive  <- sccs[sccs$groundTruth == 1, ]

null <- fitNull(negatives$logRr, negatives$seLogRr)
null

computeTraditionalP(positive$logRr, positive$seLogRr)
calibrateP(null, positive$logRr, positive$seLogRr)

model <- convertNullToErrorModel(null)
calibrateConfidenceInterval(positive$logRr, positive$seLogRr, model)

plotCalibrationEffect(negatives$logRr, negatives$seLogRr,
                      positive$logRr, positive$seLogRr)
```

## Python

```python
import empiricalcalibration as ec

sccs = ec.datasets.sccs()
negatives = sccs[sccs.groundTruth == 0]
positive = sccs[sccs.groundTruth == 1]

null = ec.fitNull(negatives.logRr, negatives.seLogRr)
print(null)

ec.computeTraditionalP(positive.logRr, positive.seLogRr)
ec.calibrateP(null, positive.logRr, positive.seLogRr)

model = ec.convertNullToErrorModel(null)
ec.calibrateConfidenceInterval(positive.logRr, positive.seLogRr, model)

ec.plotCalibrationEffect(negatives.logRr, negatives.seLogRr,
                         positive.logRr, positive.seLogRr)
```

:::

## Translation table

| R | Python |
|---|---|
| `library(EmpiricalCalibration)` | `import empiricalcalibration as ec` |
| `data(sccs)` | `sccs = ec.datasets.sccs()` |
| `df$logRr` | `df.logRr` |
| `df[df$groundTruth == 0, ]` | `df[df.groundTruth == 0]` |
| `null[1]`, `null[2]` | `null[0]`, `null[1]` — or `null["mean"]`, `null.mean` |
| `attr(cv, "alpha")` | `cv.alpha` |
| `attr(model, "LB95CI")` | `model.attributes["LB95CI"]` |
| `attr(delta, "ease1")` | `delta.attrs["ease1"]` |
| `attr(null, "mcmc")$chain` | `null.mcmc["chain"]` |
| `set.seed(42)` | `ec.set_seed(42)` |
| `print(null)` | `print(null)` |
| `ggsave(p, "f.png")` / `fileName=` | `fileName=` (unchanged) |

Indexing is the one place to be careful: R's `null[1]` is the mean, and so is
Python's `null[0]`. Name-based access avoids the trap entirely.

```{python}
import empiricalcalibration as ec

sccs = ec.datasets.sccs()
negatives = sccs[sccs.groundTruth == 0]
null = ec.fitNull(negatives.logRr, negatives.seLogRr)

print(null[0], null["mean"], null.mean)   # all the same
print(null[1], null["sd"], null.sd)
```

## Function coverage

Everything the R package exports is present.

**Null and p-values** — `fitNull`, `fitNullNonNormalLl`, `fitMcmcNull`,
`calibrateP`, `computeTraditionalP`

**Confidence intervals** — `fitSystematicErrorModel`,
`calibrateConfidenceInterval`, `computeTraditionalCi`, `convertNullToErrorModel`

**Systematic error** — `computeExpectedAbsoluteSystematicError`, `compareEase`

**MaxSPRT** — `calibrateLlr`, `computeCvPoisson`, `computeCvBinomial`,
`computeCvPoissonRegression`

**Evaluation and simulation** — `evaluateCiCalibration`, `simulateControls`,
`simulateMaxSprtData`

**Plots** — `plotForest`, `plotCalibration`, `plotCalibrationEffect`,
`plotCiCalibration`, `plotCiCalibrationEffect`, `plotCiCoverage`,
`plotErrorModel`, `plotExpectedType1Error`, `plotMcmcTrace`,
`plotTrueAndObserved`

The R package's typos are preserved where they appear in exported names, so
`normalLlApproximaton` and `closedFormIntegeralAbsolute` are spelled as in R.

## Deliberate differences

1. **Plots return a matplotlib `Figure`**, not a ggplot object. Signatures,
   colours, breaks, labels and saved dimensions are unchanged.
   `plotExpectedType1Error(showEffectSizes=True)` returns a two-panel `Figure`
   where R returns a `gtable`.

2. **`cohortMethod.groundTruth` is an integer.** In the R data it is a *factor*
   with levels `"0"`/`"1"`, while `sccs` and `caseControl` store it as a number.
   Making it an integer everywhere matches the documented format and keeps
   `df.groundTruth == 1` behaving the same across all three.

3. **`title` and `evaluation` default to `None`** rather than being R "missing"
   arguments. Passing `None` is the same as omitting them.

4. **Errors are Python exceptions.** R's `stop()` becomes `ValueError`;
   `warning()` becomes `warnings.warn(...)` with the same message text.

5. **`print()` rather than `message()`.** Notices such as "Detected data
   following normal distribution" go to stdout rather than stderr.

## Do the numbers match?

Yes, to a degree that is deliberate rather than incidental — R's optimisers,
integrator, RNG and special functions were ported rather than swapped for SciPy
equivalents, because the substitutes disagree in the third or fourth decimal.
`ec.set_seed(n)` reproduces R's `set.seed(n)` stream exactly, so stochastic
functions agree run-for-run and not merely in distribution.

The full accounting, including where and why residual differences remain, is on
the [Validation](../validation.qmd) page.

## Still using R?

The original R package is vendored in this repository under
[`extras/r-package/`](https://github.com/ablack3/EmpyriCal/tree/main/extras/r-package),
and the scripts that generate and check the R gold standard are in
[`extras/r-parity/`](https://github.com/ablack3/EmpyriCal/tree/main/extras/r-parity).
